intro.label: Introduction
intro.title: Staying Connected to Faith, Wherever You Are
intro.text:
Faith is more than a tradition. It is a connection to our roots, our families and the values passed down through generations. Hindu.international focuses on making that connection easier to maintain by helping people access spiritual services and religious practices according to their situation.

Some people want to follow their religious traditions whether they live near a sacred place or thousands of miles away. Hindu.international provides different puja, ritual and spiritual services so people can choose the services that suit their needs and stay connected to their traditions.

issue.title: What Is Anti-Conversion?
issue.text: Anti-conversion efforts seek to prevent or address religious conversion through force, coercion, fraud, deception, or unlawful inducement. The focus should be on protecting people from exploitationâ€”not preventing anyone from freely choosing or changing their religion.
issue.cardText: When religious decisions are influenced by threats, misleading promises, or exploitation of vulnerability, genuine freedom of conscience can be undermined. This can also cause emotional distress, family conflict, and concerns about cultural continuity.

respect.title: Protect Our Faith. Respect Every Person.
respect.text:
We believe Hindu heritage deserves to be understood, preserved, and respected. We encourage people to learn about Hinduism, understand their roots, and make informed choices without fear or pressure.

If a Hindu freely chooses to follow another religion, that personal choice deserves respect. We also ask everyone to discuss Hinduism and Hindu communities honestly and respectfully, without spreading false claims, insults, or hatred. Differences in belief should never become a reason to demean a community.

items.jaapIntroText:
Mahamrityunjay Jaap is the sacred chanting of the Mahamrityunjay Mantra from the Rigveda, dedicated to Lord Shiva in his form as the conqueror of death. Performed in sets of 108, 1,008, or 1,25,000 repetitions, this jaap is believed to invoke Lord Shiva's grace for health, long life, protection, and liberation from the cycle of birth and death.

Our experienced priests perform the jaap on your behalf with a proper sankalp in your name and gotra, following Vedic procedures. You receive a recorded video and prasad.
items.jaapMeaning: We worship the three-eyed Lord Shiva, who is fragrant and nourishes all beings. May He free us from the bondage of death, just as a ripened cucumber is freed from its vine, and grant us liberation.
items.jaapCol1Text: The Mahamrityunjay Mantra addresses Lord Shiva as the three-eyed one who perceives past, present and future. Chanting it with devotion is believed to create a protective shield around the devotee.
items.jaapCol2Text: This jaap is performed for the recovery of serious illness, protection from untimely death, relief from grief and fear, and to seek Lord Shiva's blessings for a long and healthy life.
items.jaapCol3Text: The Mahamrityunjay Mantra appears in the Rigveda (7.59.12) and is one of the most powerful Vedic mantras. It is chanted in temples, hospitals, and homes to invoke divine protection and spiritual healing.

jaapFaqs.a: Mahamrityunjay Jaap is the sacred repetition of the Mahamrityunjay Mantra from the Rigveda, dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is performed for health, protection, and to seek Lord Shiva's blessings.

jaapFaqs.q: How many times is the mantra chanted?
jaapFaqs.a: The jaap is offered in counts of 108, 1,008, 11,000 or 1,25,000 repetitions. The count is chosen based on your occasion and requirement.

jaapFaqs.q: Can the jaap be performed on behalf of someone else?

jaapFaqs.q: Will I receive a video of the jaap?

items.jaapIntroText:
Sundarkand is the fifth chapter of the Ramcharitmanas composed by Goswami Tulsidas and also of the Valmiki Ramayana. It narrates the journey of Lord Hanuman to Lanka to find Mata Sita, and is considered the most sacred and powerful chapter of the Ramayana. Its recitation is believed to bring courage, peace, success, and relief from difficulties.

Our priests recite the complete Sundarkand Path on your behalf with a sankalp in your name, following traditional procedures.

Known as the mother of the Vedas, it is addressed to Savitar â€” the divine sun â€” and invokes divine intelligence to illuminate the mind. The mantra is considered the essence of all Vedic wisdom and has been chanted by seekers for thousands of years.

Our Vedic priests perform the Gayatri Mantra Jaap on your behalf in complete sandhya puja procedure, with the sankalp in your name.
items.jaapMeaning: We meditate on the glorious effulgence of the divine Savitar (Sun God), who pervades the three worlds â€” earth, atmosphere, and heaven. May He illuminate and guide our intellect.
items.jaapCol1Text: The Gayatri Mantra is a 24-syllable Vedic mantra from the Rigveda, dedicated to the solar deity Savitar. It is traditionally recited at dawn, noon, and dusk in the Sandhya Vandanam ritual.
items.jaapCol2Text: Gayatri Mantra Jaap is performed for mental clarity, intelligence, academic success, spiritual progress, and to invite divine light into one's mind and life. It is especially recommended for students and seekers.
items.jaapCol3Text: The Gayatri Mantra is considered the most powerful of all Vedic mantras. Adi Shankaracharya and many sages have described its daily recitation as the highest duty of a Hindu devotee. It is the mantra of all mantras.

jaapFaqs.q: What is the Gayatri Mantra?
jaapFaqs.a: The Gayatri Mantra is a 24-syllable Vedic mantra from the Rigveda, dedicated to the divine solar deity Savitar. It is considered the mother of the Vedas and the most powerful of all Vedic mantras.

jaapFaqs.q: How many times will the mantra be chanted?

jaapFaqs.q: At what time is the jaap performed?
jaapFaqs.a: The Gayatri Mantra is traditionally recited at sunrise, noon, and sunset. We perform the jaap at sunrise (Pratah Sandhya) for maximum benefit.

The word 'Akhand' means unbroken â€” the recitation continues without pause, day and night, until all seven Kandas (chapters) are complete, typically taking 24 hours. It is considered one of the highest acts of devotion to Lord Rama.

Our team of priests performs the Akhand Ramayana Path in shifts to maintain continuous recitation, with a sankalp in your name.

jaapFaqs.q: What is Akhand Ramayana Path?
jaapFaqs.a: Akhand Ramayana Path is the continuous, uninterrupted recitation of the complete Ramcharitmanas by Tulsidas. It is completed in approximately 24 hours by a team of pandits taking turns, without breaking the chant.

jaapFaqs.q: How many pandits are needed for the path?
jaapFaqs.a: An Akhand Path typically requires a team of four to eight pandits working in shifts to maintain the continuous recitation over 24 hours.

jaapFaqs.q: Can this be arranged for a house-warming ceremony?
jaapFaqs.a: Yes. Akhand Ramayana Path is one of the most auspicious events for a grihapravesh (house-warming). It is believed to fill the new home with divine blessings from the moment of entry.

jaapFaqs.q: Will I receive a video of the recitation?
jaapFaqs.a: Yes. Key portions of the path â€” including the mangalacharan, Sundarkand, and the concluding aarti â€” are recorded and shared with you.

jaapFaqs.q: Can I book this from outside India?
jaapFaqs.a: Yes. Devotees outside India can book the Akhand Ramayana Path on their behalf by sharing their details. The path is performed at our associated temple or puja venue.
